chunks.title: PQM Agent
chunks.sub: AI agent · Engineering quality · Designer & Developer · Runs on every push
chunks.summary: An agent that checks every commit for code quality, test results, architecture health and regressions, so developers can stay on features and releases.
bullets: Designed and built the PQM Agent, which starts by itself whenever a commit is pushed and needs no manual step from the developer.
Static analysis: scans the changed code for defects and rule violations before the change reaches review.
Unit tests: runs the project's unit tests against the new commit and reports what passed and what failed.
facts: An agent that checks every commit for code quality, test results, architecture health and regressions, so developers can stay on features and releases.
Keeping code quality up is a second job on top of the real one.
Developers build features and ship releases, and quality checks get run late, by hand, or not at all.
The PQM Agent (Process Quality Management) takes that work over.
Whenever someone pushes a commit, it runs static analysis, runs the unit tests, measures the software architecture maturity (SAM) and checks that the new change has not caused a regression.
It is used across the whole organization.
Designed and built the PQM Agent, which starts by itself whenever a commit is pushed and needs no manual step from the developer.
Static analysis: scans the changed code for defects and rule violations before the change reaches review.
Unit tests: runs the project's unit tests against the new commit and reports what passed and what failed.
Software architecture maturity (SAM): measures the SAM score, so the health of the architecture is tracked on every change and not guessed at release time.
Regression check: compares the new commit with the earlier state, to catch a change that breaks something that used to work.
Rolled it out to the whole organization, so every team is held to the same checks and results can be compared across teams.
Tech stack: AI agent, Static analysis, Unit tests, SAM, Regression checks, Process quality management.

bullets: Used by 500+ engineers across the organization

facts: An agentic RAG assistant that answers questions from an organization's documents and data, and cites the exact page.
Organizations keep their knowledge in long documents, and an answer is often split across several tables or files, so people spend time searching and asking the same questions again.
The Enterprise AI Assistant is a chat assistant that answers from an organization's own documents and structured data, and shows where every answer came from.
An AI agent plans focused searches, reads what it finds, searches again if it needs more, and only then writes a cited answer.
I architected the platform end to end and led its development.
It is now used by more than 500 engineers across the organization.
Architected the platform end to end: a Next.js web app, a FastAPI service, PostgreSQL with pgvector, document storage, and open-weight models served with vLLM.

Built the agentic RAG pipeline. An agent plans focused searches, reads documents and structured data, repeats until it has the evidence, and streams an answer with numbered citations that open the exact page.

Designed hybrid retrieval: vector and full-text search merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, then rescored by a cross-encoder reranker. Table-aware chunking keeps tables intact, so questions that need two tables to answer, such as a rule in one and its exceptions in another, get answered.

Secured access by design: short-lived signed tokens between services, role-based permissions, and row-level rules so each user sees only the data they are allowed to see. Database queries are read-only, row-capped and time-limited.
Built document operations: PDF upload with duplicate detection, page preview, and an index status view that shows when documents change and need re-indexing.
Set the engineering standard: strict type checking and linting, a single migration history for the whole database, and more than 60 automated tests.
Rolled it out across the organization, where it is used by 500+ engineers.
Tech stack: AI agents, RAG, Hybrid search, Reranking, vLLM, FastAPI, Next.js, PostgreSQL + pgvector.

chunks.title: AI Test Management
chunks.summary: An LLM-based system that writes QA test cases from our UI/UX guide, then versions them through every cycle until release.
bullets: Fine-tuned a model on our application's UI and UX guide, so it learns how the product should look and behave.
Generated test cases directly from the UI/UX guide, replacing the first draft QA engineers would otherwise write by hand.

facts: An LLM-based system that writes QA test cases from our UI/UX guide, then versions them through every cycle until release.
Before an app goes to production, the organization's QA engineers test it.
They write test cases from the product, run them, and then repeat the work every cycle: which issues were fixed, what must be re-tested, and what new problems appeared.
That is slow and hard to keep organized.
This project had two parts.
The first was AI: I fine-tuned a model on our application's UI and UX guide so that it could write test cases from it.
The second was the system around the model, built with an LLM, which keeps every test case versioned and follows it through the full cycle until release.
It is used by more than 40 QA engineers.
Fine-tuned a model on our application's UI and UX guide, so it learns how the product should look and behave.
Generated test cases directly from the UI/UX guide, replacing the first draft QA engineers would otherwise write by hand.
Built the system around the model with an LLM, covering how test cases are created, stored and updated.
Added versioning: every test case and every change to it is kept, so a team can see what was tested in which cycle.
Followed the full cycle until release: tests, fixes, re-tests and new issues stay linked to the same test case.
Tech stack: LLM, Model fine-tuning, Test-case generation, Versioning, UI/UX guidelines, QA process.

facts: Interactive web views that turn Samsung 5G network data into something people can see, explore and act on.
A 5G network produces a huge amount of data, and numbers in a table are hard for people to read.
This project made that data visible.
I built web apps that present Samsung 5G network data through interactive views, so engineers can look at the network, spot what stands out and dig into it.
I worked on both sides: the React components people see and the REST APIs that deliver the data to them.
Built the frontend components that turn raw 5G network data into interactive charts and views.
Built the backend REST APIs that serve the network data to those views, with Spring Boot.
Worked across the full stack, from the data stores (MySQL and MongoDB) to the screen in React.
Used Protocol Buffers to exchange network data between services in a compact format.
Tech stack: React, Spring Boot, REST API, MySQL, MongoDB, Protocol Buffers.
